A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to produce a set of maps which are consistent with the Alfv\'enic turbulence and the primordial magnetic field (PMF).
we have presented a new method to generate CMB maps with primordial magnetic fields, which is computationally efficient.

we are able to generate the statistically isotropic CMB maps, that reproduce the $\Delta \ell =2$ correlations associated to the Alfv\'en turbulent magnetic field, and the corresponding power spectrum of the CMB temperature anisotropy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Alfv\'en mode of the magnetic field does not produce a significant imprint in the temperature anisotropy of the CMB, but it does affect polarization maps.

the non-Gaussianity in CMB anisotropy is not a sufficient condition for detection of the primordial magnetic field (PMF) and that the detection of PMF is only possible when the non-Gaussian signal is accompanied with the non-zero $\Delta \l$ correlations.
it is possible to generate sets of CMB maps, in a computationally efficient way, with the desired statistical properties, which are associated with Alfvén turbulence.
